overview: This two-page file consists of Department of State list-of-papers or index sheets concerning telephone service and telephone statistics in the Kwantung Leased Territory and neighboring parts of Manchuria. It records, rather than reproduces, consular submissions from Dairen between about 1930 and 1934, including questionnaires and statistics on government and private telephone systems, and notes the geographical coverage of reports from the Mukden and Harbin districts. The sheets also provide cross-references to related correspondence with the American Telephone and Telegraph Company and to materials filed under decimal numbers 892.75 and 893.75.

subfiles.title: List of papers on telephone service in Kwantung, entries 2a–4
subfiles.about: Indexes early correspondence and statistical forms concerning government and private telephone systems in the Kwantung Leased Territory.
subfiles.summary: The sheet describes questionnaires or forms used to collect statistical information about government and private telephone systems in the Kwantung Leased Territory and mentions a copy of an American Telephone and Telegraph Company letter dated April 21, 1930. It records Dairen despatch no. 120 A-3/8 associated with Coville and dates of October 1 and October 29, although the year is not shown. A note directs the reader to file 892.75/83 for the company's letter thanking the Dairen Consulate for the statistics it gathered.

subfiles.title: List of papers on Kwantung and Manchurian telephone statistics, entries 5–7
subfiles.about: Indexes three Dairen consular reports on telephone statistics in the Kwantung Leased Territory and wider Manchuria between 1931 and 1934.
subfiles.summary: The sheet records Langdon's Dairen despatch no. 217 of August 7, 1931, enclosing telephone statistics for the Kwantung Leased Territory, with a cross-reference to 893.75/121. It also lists a Dairen paper by Thomas, no. 18 of August 30, 1932. Vincent's despatch no. 77 of April 11, 1934, is described as covering communications in the Mukden and Harbin districts and throughout Manchuria, except for the South Manchuria Railway area, its towns, and the Kwantung Leased Territory; it is cross-referenced to 893.75/149.

interest: The file is useful less for substantive telephone data—which are not reproduced here—than as a map of where those statistics and their associated correspondence were filed. It reveals the State Department's distinctions among the Kwantung Leased Territory, the South Manchuria Railway zone, and the Mukden and Harbin reporting districts, thereby documenting the fragmented administrative geography of communications in Manchuria. The references to questionnaires, private and government systems, AT&T correspondence, and related decimal-file numbers can guide researchers to the underlying statistical reports.
